subject: Prior and posterior predictive data / analysis

messages.author: 331b448e313706ec
messages.subject: Prior and posterior predictive data / analysis
parts:
Hi there,

I know that I can use ppmc() and custom discrepancy functions for a range of procedures, but I am not sure if I can use to my advantage to achieve the following.

I am trying to do graphical ppmc as shown here: https://mc-stan.org/bayesplot/articles/graphical-ppcs.html and also analyse "prior predictives"  (graphically and using discrepancy function/residual analysis), as outlined in Schoot, R. van, Veen, D., Smeets, L., Winter, S. D., & Depaoli, S. (2020). A tutorial on using the WAMBS checklist to avoid the  misuse of Bayesian statistics. In R. van de Schoot & M. Miočevic (Eds.), Small Sample Size Solutions (pp. 30–49). Routledge.

One thing I would need is to generate simulated data using mcmc draws from a fitted model (rather than just the outcome of discrepancy functions) and based on random draws from just the model syntax (I guess I could do that using simulateData() from the lavaan package).

Is there some built-in method or an easy way to do this that I am missing? 

Thanks for your help!
Robin

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Prior and posterior predictive data / analysis
parts:
Robin

We called it discrepancy function, beause that is the original use for model evluation with residuals, fit indices etc.

But the ppmc function has general use that can applied any function that you can applied with a "normal" lavaan object, across all posterior draws.

So, for what I understand you want (data sets predicted by each posterior draws), you can use the lavPredict(fit, type="ov") lavaan function as your discFUN. This function with the "ov" argument will gives you the predicted indicator scores based on the model

Hope this helps

parts:
Robin,

About sampling from the prior: I have been meaning to make that easier for awhile. On github, I just added a new logical argument "prisamp" for sampling from the prior (only works for target="stan"). So, with pripred=TRUE, you get a blavaan object whose samples come from the priors, as opposed to the posteriors. But I still need to do some testing on it; please let me know if you have problems.

https://github.com/ecmerkle/blavaan

Ed

the solutions you proposed are working: using ppmc and lavPredict gives me the simulated/"predicted" data I want.

I'm playing around with the "prisamp" option now, so far it seems to do the job. Thanks for implementing it!

I have two follow-up questions, that you maybe can help me with: 
1) in my dataset, I have one dummy-coded exogenous variable (an experimental condition indicator) in a path analysis. Maybe this is a stupid question, but do I need to indicate this in my model specification (for example by giving it thresholds)? 2) In a similar vein, does this affect my posterior predictive model checking and/or calculation of fit indices using "blavFitIndices"? 

And maybe one last: blavaan doesn't support non-normally distributed indicator variables, right? the only way to work with non-normal data being transformations applied prior to estimation?
 
Thank you both!

parts: Robin,

On Mon, 2020-09-21 at 02:24 -0700, Robin Tschötschel wrote:
I have one dummy-coded exogenous variable (an experimental condition indicator) in a path analysis. Maybe this is a stupid question, but do I need to indicate this in my model specification (for example by giving it thresholds)?
I believe that an exogenous variable coded as 0/1 should "just work" without needing to do anything extra.
And maybe one last: blavaan doesn't support non-normally distributed indicator variables, right? the only way to work with non-normal data being transformations applied prior to estimation?

Correct, non-normal variables are not there yet. We hope to implement functionality for ordinal variables in the future. The only option for now is to export the model syntax (using mcmcfile=TRUE), then edit the jags or stan file yourself. But that would probably not be trivial.

Ed

messages.author: 331b448e313706ec
messages.subject: Re: Prior and posterior predictive data / analysis
parts:
Thanks! Good to know that feature is thought off

To get back to the prior predictives, I am now running into the following errors and warnings when calling 

ppmc(fit, thin=10, discFun=list(
    pred = function(fit) lavPredict(fit, type="ov")
)) 
for a fit object produced with prisamp=T

lavaan WARNING: some observed variances are (at least) a factor 1000 times larger than others; use varTable(fit) to investigate
lavaan WARNING: some observed variances are larger than 1000000 lavaan NOTE: use varTable(fit) to investigate

Error in lav_model_estimate(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable, : lavaan ERROR: initial model-implied matrix (Sigma) is not positive definite; check your model and/or starting parameters. 

the error doesn't always show up, but if thin is samll enough, it tends to. When it ends without error, the results look promising though!

This was on my data, I tried reproducing the error using the documentation examples. The HolzingerSwineford one doesn't even make it through calculating posterior predictives post sampling, but ends with: 

Error in chol.default(varcov) : the leading minor of order 7 is not positive definite

Best,
Robin

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Prior and posterior predictive data / analysis
parts:
Robin,

Thanks for the report. I think these warnings are related to the fact that the default blavaan priors are not very constraining and can lead to problems with positive defniteness. If you use more informative priors, I suspect that many warnings/errors will disappear. 

Alternatively, it might be possible to modify what you send to discFun in order to skip over errors. I haven't tried it to know whether it will work, but possibly

pred = function(fit){
res <- try(lavPredict(fit, type="ov"))
if(inherits(res, 'try-error')) res <- NA
res
}

Ed
